title: Signatures of a ferro-Josephson effect in twisted graphene
authors: Ruiheng Su, Zhenxiang Gao, Christopher Coleman, Manabendra Kuiri, Dacen Waters, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Matthew Yankowitz, Nemin Wei, Chunli Huang, Allan H. MacDonald, Joshua Folk
abstract: When a spin-polarized current is driven across a magnetic domain wall, the resulting spin-transfer torque could, beyond a critical threshold, set the wall's moments into precession. This precession would modulate the Berry curvature experienced by electrons traversing the wall, producing an electromotive force that is topological in nature, proportional to the precession frequency, mapping precisely onto the DC Josephson effect and leading to the name ferro-Josephson effect. We report signatures consistent with this effect in a twisted graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where spin and valley textures are linked by exchange, Hund's coupling, and spin-orbit interactions. Tuned to fillings where the isospin degeneracy is spontaneously broken, the samples develop a sharp peak in the longitudinal resistance within a fraction of a millitesla of $B_\parallel=0$---a peak that disappears as the current is reduced toward zero. In differential resistance the feature resolves into sharp resonances that disperse with $B_\parallel$ on microtesla and picoampere scales. We argue that these arise from the current-driven precession of spin-domain-wall moments, in competition with the in-plane anisotropy set by a minuscule applied field, and that they establish nonlinear transport as a sensitive probe of isospin domain-wall dynamics at energy scales far below $k_BT$.
summary: This work reports experimental signatures of a ferro-Josephson effect in twisted graphene heterostructures. The effect arises from spin-polarized currents causing domain wall precession, which modulates the Berry curvature. The evidence is presented through sharp, field-sensitive peaks in resistance measurements, establishing the material as a sensitive probe of isospin domain-wall dynamics.
main_problem: The paper reports on the observation of a ferro-Josephson effect in a twisted graphene van der Waals heterostructure.
main_result: Signatures consistent with the ferro-Josephson effect are found, characterized by a sharp peak in longitudinal resistance at zero in-plane magnetic field ($B_{\parallel}=0$) and resonant features in differential resistance.
method: Electrical transport measurements ($R_{xx}, R_{xy}, dV/dI$) are performed as a function of applied magnetic fields ($B_{\perp}, B_{\parallel}$), gate voltage, and current bias.
model_or_system: The system is a twisted graphene van der Waals heterostructure, where spin and valley textures are coupled by exchange, Hund's coupling, and spin-orbit interactions. The effect is theoretically linked to spin-transfer torque driving domain wall precession.
key_observables: Sharp peak in $R_{xx}$ at $B_{\parallel}=0$; sharp resonances in $dV/dI$; anomalous Hall effect ($R_{xy}$ hysteresis); negative in-plane magnetoresistance ($\Delta R_{xx}$).
important_parameters: Low temperatures ($T \approx 25 	ext{ mK}$); small in-plane magnetic fields ($	ext{microtesla}$ to $	ext{millitesla}$); current bias ($I_{ac}$ dependence).
main_assumptions: The observed features are interpreted as evidence for the current-driven precession of spin-domain-wall moments, which is distinct from simple depinning or Joule heating.
figures_summary: Figures map out phase diagrams ($R_{xx}$ vs. gate voltage), show $R_{xy}$ hysteresis, and provide detailed $R_{xx}(B_{\parallel})$ and $dV/dI$ spectra demonstrating the field and current dependence of the ferro-Josephson signature.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements across various magnetic field and gate voltage regimes, first establishing the anomalous Hall effect and then focusing on the current-dependent, field-sensitive features in the differential resistance to confirm the ferro-Josephson mechanism.
why_interesting: The study connects topological phenomena (Berry curvature, Josephson effect) to emergent magnetism and transport in 2D materials, providing a platform to study non-linear, current-driven quantum dynamics.
